paper.title: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces

region.name: Siftsand
region.tagline: A desert post, an endless road, and a snake who can't keep it all.

briefing: Speck. Two artefacts on my shelf. I checked them twice. They're real. Irritating.
Next: a desert post. A snake carries messages down a road that never ends.
Its belly is tiny, so it must choose what to keep. Bring me how it chooses.
You'll fail. ...I keep saying that. Go.
reminder: Still here? The road won't get shorter, Speck. It never ends. That's the point.
Read the book. Most of a desert is just sand.
return: An hourglass. The neck opens for beads and pinches shut for sand. Hm. HMPH.
Three for three, Speck. That stopped being luck at two.
On the shelf. Three in a row... Something's taking shape up there. Something big.

arrival: Siftsand: a desert post where the Endless Road begins. It never ends. Ever.
Noodle the snake carries the message beads. He also swallows every grain of sand.
resolution: Noodle gulps a ruby, lets the sand slide by, and grins. Belly never full.
Penny stamps a tiny parcel DELIVERED. Inside: an hourglass. 'For your giant.'

inhabitants.name: Noodle
inhabitants.role: Giver of c1. The outpost's courier, a very long green sand snake with one small belly (the fixed-size state). He gulps every grain the same way (time-invariant), so at the bell he can only say mush. Sweet, burpy, easily excited; his happy loop-de-loop after c1 pops a vertebra (sets up c2).

default: Sssorry, can't chat. Too full of sand. *burp* ...that was a pebble.
afterSolved: Beads in, sand out! I'm a picky eater now.
Doc Marrow says no more loop-de-loops. I say: never say never.

inhabitants.name: Tumble
inhabitants.role: Flavour, and the region's curious kid: rides on Noodle's tail and asks everyone 'why'. A natural giver for later fundamentals (hidden state, exponential decay, sigmoid/softplus, linear projections). Never explains anything.

default: I'm Tumble! I ride on Noodle's tail. I have SO many questions. Like, why is sand?
His belly gurgles in colours. Mostly the colour of sand.
afterSolved: Noodle says ruby, lapis, emerald now! Next I'm teaching him 'please'.

inhabitants.name: Kayvee
inhabitants.role: Red herring and flavour: a pack-rat who never chooses and keeps every letter forever (attention's KV cache: no compression, so each lookup gets slower as the pile grows; Section 3.1). His door no longer shuts.

default: Why choose? I keep EVERY letter. Every single one. Forever!
Finding one takes a bit longer every day. And my door won't shut.
afterSolved: Noodle keeps one bellyful and still beats me. I'm having a yard sale.

inhabitants.name: Doc Marrow
inhabitants.role: Giver of c2. The outpost's bone-setter in light-blue scrubs. Has every part for Noodle's new vertebra, but chewed the drawing. Professional, mostly. Points the player to the Belly Scanner (c3) after c2.

default: Bone-setter. I set bones. Sometimes I chew them. Occupational hazard.
afterSolved: Identical vertebrae, stacked all the way down. Lovely spine. Not chewing it.

inhabitants.name: Penny
inhabitants.role: Giver of c4 (explain). The postmistress, proud of her one big rubber stamp that prints a whole road at once and treats every grain alike: an LTI SSM / global convolution in a post-office cap. Skeptical of the 'fussy' snake.

default: Post office. My one stamp prints a whole road at once. Every grain alike. Fast!
A snake for a postman? Hmph. Come back when that scanner agrees with him.
afterSolved: My old stamp is framed now. Wonderful on straight roads. Only straight roads.

inhabitants.name: Umberto
inhabitants.role: Comic relief by the oasis water: says 'um' all the time, a walking filler token (the paper's 'um' example in Section 3.5.2). Noodle used to swallow every um.

default: Um. Hi. Um. I tell Noodle stories. Um. He swallows every um.
afterSolved: Um. Noodle doesn't swallow my ums anymore. Um. Rude. Um. Fair.

challenges.title: Gulp or Let Go

spec.title: Gulp or Let Go
spec.controlsHint: Set Δ B C per grain · ⛓ links columns · ▶ run
spec.math: Per road, belly h = [0, 0, 0] (one channel per colour, N = 1 each). For each tile t in order: k = tokens[tile].kind; Δ = knobs[k].delta; Abar = exp(A*Δ) = exp(-Δ); Bbar = (exp(A*Δ) - 1) / A * knobs[k].B = (1 - exp(-Δ)) * knobs[k].B (zero-order hold, Eq. 4, with A = -1); h = Abar*h + Bbar*color(tile), per channel; voice y_t = knobs[k].C * h. Draw the belly as rgb(h) and the voice as rgb(y), each channel clamped to [0, 1] for display only.
judge: At every bell tile: target = colour of the most recent bead before it on the same road (every bell has one). err = max over channels |y - target|.
ok if err <= tolerance. Otherwise: silent if max|y| <= tolerance; else s = dot(y, target) / dot(target, target), r = y - s*target: faded if max|r| <= tolerance and s < 1; else mush.
At every non-bell tile: chatty if max|y| > tolerance (tag only the first such tile per road).
spec.winCondition: Every bell on all three roads is ok and no road is chatty.

solution.allWinning: Exactly 8 settings win (checked by brute force over all 8000): bead Δ=10, B=1, C=0; sand Δ=0.001, B=0 or 1, C=0; bell Δ=0.001 or 0.01, B=0 or 1, C=1. No chained (identical-column) setting can win.
solution.rule: Section 3.5.2: a large Δ resets the state and focuses on the current input (beads); a small Δ persists the state and ignores the input (sand, bells); B lets an input into the state, C lets the state out (only at bells). The rule must depend on the grain: selection, not time invariance.

challenges.design: A long sand-coloured paper board titled spec.title, spec.controlsHint along the top, ✕ top right calls api.onClose(). LEFT: the three roads of spec.roads as rows of small paper tiles, one tile per character (spec.roadCode): beads are faceted gems in their token colour, sand is a pale dot, bells are small ink-dark bells. Each road has a little green paper snake head at its left end with a round belly bubble beside it (a tiny 'A = −1' plaque on the bubble, tooltip only). RIGHT: the knob panel, three columns for spec.kinds (icons only, tooltips from tip). Each column: a Δ dial stepping through spec.knobs.delta.options (◀ ▶ or mouse wheel; shows the number), a B toggle (0/1, a closed/open mouth) and a C toggle (0/1, a closed/open speech bubble); row labels Δ, B, C with tooltips step/in/out. Above the columns a ⛓ button (tooltip 'same for all'). Start from spec.initial. While chained, changing a knob in any column sets that knob in all three (one rule for every grain); clicking ⛓ unchains them (values kept), clicking again re-chains them (the last-changed column is copied to the others). A big ▶ runs all three roads at once (clicking ▶ again mid-run skips to the end): each snake slides tile by tile (about 120 ms per tile), its belly bubble shows rgb(h), a thin ribbon swatch of rgb(h) is left under every tile it passes, and whenever max|y| > spec.tolerance a small speech bubble of colour rgb(y) pops above that tile (all values from spec.math). Then spec.judge tags every bell with ✓ or a spec.feedback word (…, faded, mush) and puts a red 'chatty' tag on the first off-bell tile where a snake talks. Win (spec.winCondition): the snakes wiggle, api.sfx('success'), spec.successText, api.onSolved() exactly once, then a ↩ button closes. Failure: api.sfx('fail') and a small shake; tags stay until the next change; never say which knob is wrong. From the 3rd failed run, show spec.hintAfterFailures.text in a corner. Runs are unlimited; nothing resets on failure.

I gulp every grain the same. So at the bell, all I can say is mush.
Set my gulps for me? Beads, sand, bells. It's all in the old book.

challenges.title: The Belly Scanner
challenges.prompt:
## The Belly Scanner

*Follow Noodle grain by grain, exactly as the book says.*

numpy, `float64`. A loop over time is fine.

### 1. `selective_scan(x, delta, A, B, C, h0=None)`
The SSM of **Eq. (2a)/(2b)**, time-varying as in **Algorithm 2**, discretized by the **ZOH of Eq. (4)**.

- `x`: `(L, D)` grains; `delta`: `(L, D)`, all > 0 (one Δ per step and channel)
- `A`: `(D, N)`, all < 0; row `d` is the diagonal of channel `d`'s A
- `B`, `C`: `(L, N)`, one row per step, shared by all channels
- `h0`: `(D, N)` belly before step 0; `None` = zeros
- Channel `d` runs its own SSM with an `N`-long state `h[d]`, using `A[d]`, `delta[t, d]`, `B[t]`, `C[t]`
- `y[t, d] = C[t] · h_t[d]` (sum over the `N` pockets)
- **returns** `(y, h_last)`: `y` `(L, D)`; `h_last` `(D, N)` = the state after the last step

### 2. `s6(x, A, W_B, W_C, w_delta, delta_bias)`
The selection mechanism (**Section 3.2**, **Algorithm 2**), then `selective_scan` from a zero belly.

- `x`: `(L, D)`; `A`: `(D, N)`; `W_B`, `W_C`: `(D, N)`; `w_delta`, `delta_bias`: `(D,)`
- `B = x @ W_B`, `C = x @ W_C` (s_B, s_C = Linear_N, no bias)
- `Δ = τ_Δ(Parameter + s_Δ(x))` with Parameter = `delta_bias`, `s_Δ(x) = Broadcast_D(Linear_1(x))`, `Linear_1(x) = x @ w_delta`, and τ_Δ as Section 3.2 chooses
- **returns** `y` `(L, D)`

Run the tests. The hourglasses only flip when every test passes.
challenges.starterCode:
import numpy as np


def selective_scan(x, delta, A, B, C, h0=None):
    """THE BELLY SCANNER: Noodle's belly, grain by grain (Eq. 2, ZOH Eq. 4, Algorithm 2).

    x: (L, D)  delta: (L, D) > 0  A: (D, N) < 0  B, C: (L, N)  h0: (D, N) or None
    returns (y, h_last): y (L, D), h_last (D, N)
    """
    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=np.float64)
    A = np.asarray(A, dtype=np.float64)
    L, D = x.shape
    N = A.shape[1]
    # TODO: the hourglasses are empty. The scanner shows nothing at all.
    return np.zeros((L, D)), np.zeros((D, N))


def s6(x, A, W_B, W_C, w_delta, delta_bias):
    """THE CHOOSER: Δ, B, C made from the grains themselves (Section 3.2, Algorithm 2).

    x: (L, D)  A: (D, N)  W_B, W_C: (D, N)  w_delta: (D,)  delta_bias: (D,)  ->  y (L, D)
    """
    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=np.float64)
    # TODO: Noodle chooses nothing yet.
    return np.zeros_like(x)
challenges.tests:
import numpy as np


def _scan(*args, **kwargs):
    out = selective_scan(*args, **kwargs)
    assert isinstance(out, (tuple, list)) and len(out) == 2, "selective_scan must return a pair: (y, h_last)"
    return np.asarray(out[0], dtype=np.float64), np.asarray(out[1], dtype=np.float64)


def _s6(*args):
    return np.asarray(s6(*args), dtype=np.float64)


def test_one_grain_by_hand():
    ln2 = np.log(2.0)
    x, delta, A, B, C = [[2.0]], [[ln2]], [[-1.0]], [[1.0]], [[1.0]]
    y, h = _scan(np.array(x), np.array(delta), np.array(A), np.array(B), np.array(C))
    assert y.shape == (1, 1), f"one grain, one channel: y must have shape (L, D) = (1, 1), got {y.shape}"
    assert h.shape == (1, 1), f"h_last must have shape (D, N) = (1, 1), got {h.shape}"
    assert np.all(np.isfinite(y)), "the belly is nan/inf after a single friendly grain"
    if np.allclose(y, [[2.0 * ln2]], atol=1e-6):
        raise AssertionError("A shortcut! That B̄ is only approximately right. Eq. (4) gives the exact rule.")
    if np.allclose(y, [[2.0]], atol=1e-6):
        raise AssertionError("B went into the belly raw. Eq. (4) discretizes B too, not only A.")
    assert np.allclose(y, [[1.0]], atol=1e-9), "one grain (x = 2, Δ = ln 2, A = -1, B = C = 1): wrong belly. Re-read Eq. (4)."
    assert np.allclose(h, [[1.0]], atol=1e-9), "h_last must be the state after the last step"
    y2, h2 = _scan(np.array(x), np.array(delta), np.array(A), np.array(B), np.array(C), h0=np.array([[4.0]]))
    assert np.allclose(y2, [[3.0]], atol=1e-9) and np.allclose(h2, [[3.0]], atol=1e-9), (
        "starting from h0 = 4 the belly is wrong: h0 is the state *before* step 0")


def test_two_pockets_two_steps_by_hand():
    ln2 = np.log(2.0)
    x = np.array([[1.0], [3.0]])
    delta = np.array([[ln2], [ln2]])
    A = np.array([[-1.0, -2.0]])
    B = np.array([[1.0, 2.0], [0.0, 1.0]])
    C = np.array([[1.0, 1.0], [2.0, -1.0]])
    y, h = _scan(x, delta, A, B, C)
    assert y.shape == (2, 1), f"L = 2, D = 1: y must have shape (2, 1), got {y.shape}"
    assert h.shape == (1, 2), f"D = 1, N = 2: h_last must have shape (1, 2), got {h.shape}"
    if np.allclose(y, [[2.0794415416798357], [-1.732867951399863]], atol=1e-6):
        raise AssertionError("A shortcut! That B̄ is only approximately right. Eq. (4) gives the exact rule.")
    assert np.allclose(y, [[1.25], [-0.8125]], atol=1e-9), (
        "one channel, two belly pockets (N = 2), two steps: wrong y. Each step t uses its own B_t and C_t, "
        "each pocket its own A, and y_t adds up every pocket.")
    assert np.allclose(h, [[0.25, 1.3125]], atol=1e-9), "h_last must be the state after the last step"


def test_theorem_1_the_old_gate_inside():
    rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
    L, D = 12, 3
    g = rng.uniform(0.02, 0.98, size=(L, D))
    delta = -np.log1p(-g)  # picked so that the gate of Theorem 1 is exactly g
    x = rng.normal(size=(L, D))
    y, h = _scan(x, delta, -np.ones((D, 1)), np.ones((L, 1)), np.ones((L, 1)))
    assert y.shape == (L, D), f"expected y of shape {(L, D)}, got {y.shape}"
    assert h.shape == (D, 1), f"expected h_last of shape {(D, 1)}, got {h.shape}"
    want = np.zeros((L, D))
    s = np.zeros(D)
    for t in range(L):
        s = (1.0 - g[t]) * s + g[t] * x[t]
        want[t] = s
    assert np.allclose(y, want, atol=1e-10), (
        "Theorem 1: with N = 1, A = -1, B = 1 (and C = 1) the scan must become the gated recurrence (5), "
        "h_t = (1 - g_t) h_(t-1) + g_t x_t. Appendix C shows why.")
    assert np.allclose(h[:, 0], want[-1], atol=1e-10), "h_last must be the state after the last step"


def test_big_step_starts_fresh():
    rng = np.random.default_rng(4)
    L, D, N = 9, 3, 4
    A = -np.tile(np.arange(1, N + 1, dtype=np.float64), (D, 1))  # S4D-Real: A_n = -(n + 1)
    x = rng.normal(size=(L, D))
    delta = rng.uniform(0.05, 0.6, size=(L, D))
    delta[5] = 60.0
    B = rng.normal(size=(L, N))
    C = rng.normal(size=(L, N))
    y, _ = _scan(x, delta, A, B, C, h0=rng.normal(size=(D, N)))
    x2 = x.copy()
    x2[:5] = rng.normal(size=(5, D)) * 3.0
    y2, _ = _scan(x2, delta, A, B, C, h0=rng.normal(size=(D, N)))
    assert y.shape == (L, D), f"expected y of shape {(L, D)}, got {y.shape}"
    assert np.all(np.isfinite(y)), "a big Δ made the belly nan/inf"
    assert not np.allclose(y[:5], y2[:5]), "before step 5, different grains (and a different h0) must give a different belly"
    assert np.allclose(y[5:], y2[5:], atol=1e-9), (
        "a huge Δ at step 5: everything before it (grains and h0) should no longer matter from step 5 on")


def test_tiny_step_lets_a_grain_slide_by():
    rng = np.random.default_rng(5)
    L, D, N = 8, 2, 3
    A = -rng.uniform(0.5, 2.0, size=(D, N))
    x = rng.normal(size=(L, D))
    delta = rng.uniform(0.1, 1.0, size=(L, D))
    delta[3] = 1e-9
    B = rng.normal(size=(L, N))
    C = rng.normal(size=(L, N))
    y, _ = _scan(x, delta, A, B, C)
    assert np.all(np.isfinite(y)), "a tiny Δ made the belly nan/inf"
    x2 = x.copy()
    x2[3] += 1000.0
    y2, _ = _scan(x2, delta, A, B, C)
    assert np.allclose(y, y2, atol=1e-4), "a tiny Δ at step 3: making that grain 1000 bigger should barely change anything"
    x3 = x.copy()
    x3[2] += 1.0
    y3, _ = _scan(x3, delta, A, B, C)
    assert not np.allclose(y[4:], y3[4:]), "with a tiny Δ at step 3, the belly from step 2 must still be carried past it"


def test_never_peeks_down_the_road():
    rng = np.random.default_rng(6)
    L, D, N = 10, 3, 2
    A = -rng.uniform(0.5, 2.0, size=(D, N))
    x = rng.normal(size=(L, D))
    delta = rng.uniform(0.1, 1.0, size=(L, D))
    B = rng.normal(size=(L, N))
    C = rng.normal(size=(L, N))
    y, _ = _scan(x, delta, A, B, C)
    x2, d2, B2, C2 = x.copy(), delta.copy(), B.copy(), C.copy()
    x2[6:] += 5.0
    d2[6:] *= 3.0
    B2[6:] -= 2.0
    C2[6:] += 1.0
    y2, _ = _scan(x2, d2, A, B2, C2)
    assert np.allclose(y[:6], y2[:6], atol=1e-12), "changing grains 6.. changed the belly at steps 0..5: the scanner peeked ahead"
    assert not np.allclose(y[6:], y2[6:]), "steps 6.. should notice their own changed grains"


def test_long_road_in_two_chunks():
    rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
    L, D, N = 12, 3, 4
    A = -rng.uniform(0.3, 3.0, size=(D, N))
    x = rng.normal(size=(L, D))
    delta = rng.uniform(0.05, 1.0, size=(L, D))
    B = rng.normal(size=(L, N))
    C = rng.normal(size=(L, N))
    y, h = _scan(x, delta, A, B, C)
    assert y.shape == (L, D) and h.shape == (D, N), f"expected shapes {(L, D)} and {(D, N)}, got {y.shape} and {h.shape}"
    assert np.max(np.abs(y)) > 1e-3, "the belly stays empty on a long, busy road"
    ya, ha = _scan(x[:5], delta[:5], A, B[:5], C[:5])
    yb, hb = _scan(x[5:], delta[5:], A, B[5:], C[5:], h0=ha)
    assert np.allclose(np.concatenate([ya, yb]), y, atol=1e-10), (
        "the road scanned in two chunks (h_last of the first fed in as h0 of the second) must match one long scan")
    assert np.allclose(hb, h, atol=1e-10), "after two chunks, h_last must match the one long scan's h_last"


def test_belly_is_linear_in_the_grains():
    rng = np.random.default_rng(8)
    L, D, N = 7, 2, 3
    A = -rng.uniform(0.5, 2.0, size=(D, N))
    delta = rng.uniform(0.05, 1.0, size=(L, D))
    B = rng.normal(size=(L, N))
    C = rng.normal(size=(L, N))
    x1 = rng.normal(size=(L, D))
    x2 = rng.normal(size=(L, D))
    y1, _ = _scan(x1, delta, A, B, C)
    y2, _ = _scan(x2, delta, A, B, C)
    y12, _ = _scan(2.0 * x1 - 3.0 * x2, delta, A, B, C)
    assert np.max(np.abs(y1)) > 1e-3, "the belly stays empty"
    assert np.allclose(y12, 2.0 * y1 - 3.0 * y2, atol=1e-9), (
        "with Δ, B and C held fixed the recurrence (2) is linear in x: scanning 2·x1 - 3·x2 must give 2·y1 - 3·y2")


def test_a_whole_road_by_the_book():
    x = np.array([[-0.9, -0.63], [0.74, -0.71], [-0.52, -1.61], [-0.37, -1.03], [-0.64, 2.88]])
    delta = np.array([[1.14, 1.25], [0.7, 1.17], [1.08, 1.37], [1.1, 1.07], [0.4, 0.76]])
    A = np.array([[-2.64, -0.59, -2.74], [-1.77, -1.32, -1.2]])
    B = np.array([[1.28, 0.44, -0.12], [1.32, 0.0, 0.62], [-0.44, 0.3, -0.74], [-0.9, 1.11, -0.42], [2.12, 1.23, -0.93]])
    C = np.array([[1.39, -0.65, 0.53], [0.19, -1.13, -0.27], [-0.45, -0.63, -0.27], [0.78, -0.09, 0.97], [-0.49, 1.91, 0.39]])
    y, h = _scan(x, delta, A, B, C)
    assert y.shape == (5, 2) and h.shape == (2, 3), f"expected shapes (5, 2) and (2, 3), got {y.shape} and {h.shape}"
    assert np.allclose(y, [[-0.343057331522, -0.427752532804], [0.252449194484, 0.0147556825409], [0.0697493729232, -0.149690733504], [0.19729209814, 0.904597158158], [-1.01855110296, 0.973718384743]], atol=1e-8), (
        "a whole road (L = 5, D = 2, N = 3): wrong y. Per step: Δ_t per channel, Ā and B̄ from Eq. (4), "
        "then the state update, then the read-out with C_t.")
    assert np.allclose(h, [[-0.291869169639, -0.641833832928, 0.164963140542], [2.67935468128, 1.43142400799, -1.14722481202]], atol=1e-8), "a whole road: wrong h_last"


def test_s6_chooses_by_the_book():
    x = np.array([[0.5, -1.0], [1.5, 0.25], [-0.75, 2.0], [0.0, -0.5]])
    A = np.array([[-1.0, -2.0], [-0.5, -3.0]])
    W_B = np.array([[0.8, -0.3], [0.2, 0.6]])
    W_C = np.array([[-0.4, 1.1], [0.7, 0.5]])
    w_delta = np.array([1.2, -0.9])
    delta_bias = np.array([-0.5, 0.3])
    y = _s6(x, A, W_B, W_C, w_delta, delta_bias)
    assert y.shape == (4, 2), f"s6 must return y of shape (L, D) = (4, 2), got {y.shape}"
    assert np.all(np.isfinite(y)), "s6 returned nan/inf on a small, friendly road"
    assert np.allclose(y, [[-0.0744921831255, 0.236877087446], [-0.995520042995, -0.173355165481], [2.28072866683, 0.475441213599], [-0.22905220853, -0.0802864107894]], atol=1e-8), (
        "s6 on a small road: wrong y. Check B = x @ W_B, C = x @ W_C, and Δ: Parameter plus the broadcast "
        "Linear_1(x), passed through τ_Δ (Section 3.2 names it).")


def test_s6_one_choice_for_every_channel():
    rng = np.random.default_rng(9)
    L, D, N = 8, 3, 2
    A = -np.tile(np.array([1.0, 2.0]), (D, 1))
    W_B = rng.normal(size=(D, N))
    W_C = rng.normal(size=(D, N))
    w_delta = np.array([60.0, 0.0, 0.0])  # only channel 0 (the marker) feeds Linear_1
    delta_bias = np.array([-1.0, -0.5, 0.0])
    x = rng.normal(size=(L, D))
    x[:, 0] = 0.0
    x[4, 0] = 1.0  # a marker grain at step 4
    y = _s6(x, A, W_B, W_C, w_delta, delta_bias)
    assert y.shape == (L, D), f"expected y of shape {(L, D)}, got {y.shape}"
    assert np.all(np.isfinite(y)), "s6 returned nan/inf"
    x2 = x.copy()
    x2[:4, 1:] = rng.normal(size=(4, D - 1)) * 2.0
    y2 = _s6(x2, A, W_B, W_C, w_delta, delta_bias)
    assert not np.allclose(y[:4], y2[:4]), "different grains before the marker should give a different belly"
    assert np.allclose(y[4:], y2[4:], atol=1e-9), (
        "the marker at step 4 must make every channel start fresh, even channels whose own value there is ordinary. "
        "Re-read how s_Δ(x) is built (Section 3.2, and the end of Section 3.5.1).")

challenges.title: The Old Stamp
challenges.question: Why can't my stamp carry scattered beads? What does Noodle do instead, and why can't he use my stamp?
rubric: Time invariance (Section 2, 'Linear Time Invariance', Eqs. 2-3): the stamp is an LTI SSM / global convolution: its parameters (Δ, A, B, C, hence A_bar, B_bar) are the same at every step, so every token is processed identically whatever it is; the whole layer is one fixed kernel K = (CB_bar, CA_barB_bar, ..., CA_bar^k B_bar, ...) applied as y = x * K.

Copying versus Selective Copying (Section 3.1, Figure 2, Section 4.1.1): on the ordinary Copying task the spacing between inputs and outputs is constant, so tracking time alone (e.g. a kernel of exactly the right length) solves it; in Selective Copying the spacing is random, so what to keep must be decided from the content, and a static kernel cannot model varying spacing (Table 1: S4 18.3% vs S6 97.0% without gating).

Selection (Section 3.2, Algorithm 2): Mamba makes Δ, B and C functions of the current input (B and C linear projections of x; Δ = softplus of a parameter plus a projection of x), so the dynamics change token by token (time-varying).

What the input-dependent Δ does (Section 3.5.2, Theorem 1): a large Δ resets the state and focuses on the current input (keep the bead), a small Δ keeps the state and ignores the current input (let sand pass); B controls what enters the state and C what is read out.

The price (Sections 3.2-3.3, Appendix D): with time-varying parameters the model is no longer equivalent to a convolution, so the fast convolution mode is lost; Mamba computes the recurrence with a parallel scan in a hardware-aware fused kernel (expanded state kept in fast SRAM, recomputed in the backward pass), still linear in sequence length.
challenges.passBar: Pass if at least 3 of the 5 criteria are clearly met and criteria 2 and 4 are both among them. Fail regardless of the count if the answer reverses Δ (says a large Δ ignores the input or a small Δ resets the state), claims LTI or convolutional models cannot solve the ordinary Copying task, says selective SSMs are still computed as a convolution, or credits architectural gating alone with solving Selective Copying.

artefact.name: The Sifting Hourglass
artefact.description: A pocket hourglass with a tiny snake coiled on top. Its neck opens wide for beads and pinches shut for sand, so its one small bulb keeps only what matters.
artefact.look: A small hourglass (about 0.6 units tall): two clear glass cones meeting at a narrow neck, warm wooden caps top and bottom, a little cone of golden sand in the lower bulb. A green paper snake coils around the top cap with its head raised. Idle: it turns slowly; sand trickles, the neck pinches and the trickle stops, then a coloured bead drops through.

guard: Do not say what Δ does (a large Δ resets the state and focuses on the current input; a small Δ keeps the state and ignores the input), what Δ → ∞ or Δ → 0 means, or which Δ, B or C a bead, a sand grain or a bell needs.
Do not say that B controls what enters the state and C what is read out of it, or when either should be 0 or 1.
Do not say whether the knobs should be the same for every grain or chosen per grain (time-invariant versus selective).
Do not explain Theorem 1's gate in words or symbols (g_t = σ(Linear(x_t)), h_t = (1 - g_t) h_(t-1) + g_t x_t) or what g_t → 0 or g_t → 1 does.

Do not describe the Mamba block of Figure 3 / Section 3.4: which pieces sit in which branch, their order (Conv, σ, SSM), the σ on the second branch, the multiplicative join, the input and output projections. Do not write Eq. (4) out for a diagonal A (B_bar = (exp(ΔA) - 1)/A · B), and do not say whether B_bar equals Δ·B.
Do not say that τ_Δ is softplus, or how s_Δ(x) is built and broadcast over the D channels.
Never write scan or s6 code or pseudo-code: no per-step update with A_bar_t, B_bar_t, C_t, no read-out formula, nothing on carrying the last state into the next chunk.

Do not explain why time-invariant (LTI) models fail on Selective Copying (constant versus random spacing, static kernels, content-awareness), or that selection breaks the convolution view and forces a scan.

offlineHints.text: The step decides: linger, or let it pass. Section 3.5.2 reads it plainly. Theorem 1 reads it twice.
One letter lets in. One lets out. The last lines of 3.5.2 know which is which.
Who treats every grain alike learns nothing of grains. Section 2 names this habit. Algorithm 2 breaks it.
Straight roads and scattered roads. Figure 2 draws both. Section 3.1 says why one is harder.
Bones stack in one shape, again and again. Figure 3 draws three shapes. Only one is a snake.
Weigh the projections, not the snake. Section 3.4 counts them in D squared.
Continuous becomes discrete by a rule with a name. Equation 4 holds it. Hold the grain the whole step.
The belly is carried grain by grain. Equations 2a and 2b, with a little t on every letter.
What chooses the step? Algorithm 2, line four. Then the sentence after it in Section 3.2.
Long roads are walked in pieces. Appendix D says what must be carried from one piece to the next.
A stamp needs a rule that never changes. Section 3.3 says what replaced it. Appendix D says how.
An old gate sleeps inside the new snake. Theorem 1 wakes it. Appendix C shows its bones.
